questions.q: Does an IMEI primarily identify the telecommunication subscriber (the user) or the actual physical mobile equipment?
options: It exclusively identifies the physical hardware equipment
It exclusively identifies the subscriber billing account
It identifies the network's local cell tower
It identifies the specific phone number attached to the SIM
questions.explain: IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) uniquely identifies the handset/hardware. The SIM and IMSI identify the subscriber.

questions.q: At a core technological level, what defines the difference between GSM and CDMA networking?
options: GSM uses wired connections, whereas CDMA is entirely wireless
GSM separates channels strictly by unique encryption codes, while CDMA uses standard SIM cards for timing
GSM primarily divides transmission by distinct time slots and frequencies (TDMA/FDMA), while CDMA uses mathematical spread-spectrum codes across the same frequency
GSM operates only on 1900MHz, while CDMA operates only on 900MHz
questions.explain: GSM and CDMA are competing original network standards. GSM uses Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA), isolating users by time and frequency. CDMA isolates users via code division.

questions.q: Why do telecom engineers implement the 1800MHz GSM band in densely populated city areas rather than relying exclusively on the 900MHz band?
options: Because 1800MHz penetrates thick concrete walls more effectively than 900MHz
Because the 1800MHz band naturally prevents unauthorized eavesdropping
Because higher frequencies like 1800MHz provide more available bandwidth to handle a higher capacity of simultaneous calls
Because older feature phones are not technically compatible with 900MHz
questions.explain: Higher frequency bands (1800/1900MHz) cover shorter distances but offer a larger spectrum slice, thereby granting vastly superior user capacity in dense urban centers.

questions.q: If a user forgets their PIN, inputs it wrong 3 times, and then subsequently inputs the PUK code incorrectly 10 consecutive times, what is the exact hardware consequence?
options: The mobile phone processor burns out and must be replaced
The SIM card is permanently disabled/ruined and must be physically replaced by the provider
The network temporarily suspends the account for 24 hours
The phone prompts for an administrator recovery password to unlock the SIM
questions.explain: A strict security feature of the GSM standard is that 10 wrong PUK attempts permanently fry or 'brick' the SIM chip to prevent unauthorized cloning or access.

questions.q: What is the fixed, standard digit length of a Personal Unblocking Key (PUK) code?
questions.explain: Standard PIN codes are generally 4 digits, but the Personal Unblocking Key (PUK) is mandated by GSM specifications to be an 8-digit numerical code.

questions.q: How many digits typically comprise a standard IMEI number assigned to a mobile phone?

questions.q: At a hardware level, how does an OTG cable physically signal a mobile device's charging port to switch from acting as a 'client' to a 'USB Host'?
options: It applies 12 volts to the power pin
It grounds the micro-USB/USB-C ID pin, notifying the controller chip to supply power outwards
It sends a USSD code through the data line
It reverses the polarity of the data pins (D+ and D-)
questions.explain: An OTG (On-The-Go) cable features a wired short between the ID (Sense) pin and the Ground pin. The smartphone detects this short and transitions to acting as the USB Host.

questions.explain: To seamlessly roam between European/African grids (900/1800MHz) and American grids (850/1900MHz), quad-band devices support all four major GSM bands: 850, 900, 1800, and 1900 MHz.

questions.q: Historically, what primary hardware trait distinguished original CDMA network devices from standard GSM devices regarding user subscriber identity?
options: Original CDMA phones natively lacked removable SIM cards, with subscriber identity flashed directly into the phone's memory
Original CDMA devices utilized dual SIM card slots exclusively
Original CDMA devices used paper voucher cards for identity instead of microchips
Original CDMA devices required physically plugging the phone into a wall to swap users
questions.explain: While GSM mandated the Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) for portability, original CDMA networks (like Verizon/Sprint initially) programmed the Electronic Serial Number (ESN) directly, requiring carrier intervention to switch handsets.

questions.q: The acronym USSD, famously used for strings like *#06#, stands for which of the following terms?
questions.explain: USSD stands for Unstructured Supplementary Service Data, a protocol used by GSM phones to communicate with service providers.

questions.q: What fundamental networking mechanism defines the technological difference between USSD operations and SMS messaging?
options: USSD is restricted to internet connectivity, while SMS works over pure cellular waves
USSD establishes a responsive real-time open session between phone and server, while SMS employs a 'store-and-forward' methodology
SMS sends commands directly to cell towers, while USSD only interfaces directly with SIM files
SMS requires the input of the '#' symbol to function, unlike USSD
questions.explain: A USSD query opens an immediate two-way live session with the provider's server (crucial for menus/balances), whereas SMS sends messages that wait at a server center until the recipient device is available (store-and-forward).

The folding hinge inherently contained dual GSM antennas for double network reception
The mechanical folding motion acted to manually charge the battery slightly each time
They inherently operated purely on 1900MHz frequency bandwidth

questions.q: If a subscriber imports a simple dual-band 'feature phone' manufactured exclusively to support 900MHz and 1800MHz from Nigeria to the United States, what failure will almost certainly occur?
options: The USSD interface will revert exclusively to the French language
The device's power charger will blow a fuse instantly upon entry
The device will fail to locate cellular signal because the USA primarily employs 850MHz and 1900MHz bands
The phone will force the CDMA protocol to override GSM automatically
questions.explain: Because North America traditionally uses the 850MHz and 1900MHz bands, older hardware only equipped with European/African dual-band modems (900/1800MHz) lack the physical antennas/chips to communicate with US cell towers.
